formats.key: depositForBurn(uint256 amount, uint32 destinationDomain, bytes32 mintRecipient, address burnToken, bytes32 destinationCaller, uint256 maxFee, uint32 minFinalityThreshold)
effects: `amount` of burnToken (USDC) moves from the signer to the local TokenMinter through transferFrom, using the signer's allowance to TokenMessengerV2, and is burned on Polygon.
On destinationDomain, mintRecipient (bytes32) is minted `amount` minus the fee charged. The fee is capped by maxFee and must be less than amount.
Only destinationCaller can relay the message on the destination chain. bytes32(0) means anyone can.
minFinalityThreshold sets fast or standard attestation. This changes the speed and the fee charged, which stays within maxFee.
formats.shown: Bridge <amount USDC> to domain <number>, with the amount, the raw domain number, the raw bytes32 mint recipient, the max fee in USDC and the raw bytes32 destination caller.

findings.title: depositForBurn: destination domain shown as a bare CCTP number (0, 3, 6) instead of a chain name.
findings.evidence: descriptor definitions.destination {"label":"CCTP dest. domain","format":"raw"}; interpolatedIntent "Bridge {amount} to domain {destinationDomain}". Case 2 screen: "Bridge 100 USDC to domain 6" (Base). Case 3: "domain 0" (Ethereum).
findings.fix: Add $.metadata.enums.cctpDomain (0 Ethereum, 1 Avalanche, 2 OP Mainnet, 3 Arbitrum, 5 Solana, 6 Base, 7 Polygon PoS, …) and use format enum, so the sentence reads "Bridge 100 USDC to Base".

findings.title: depositForBurn: the intent says the full amount is bridged, but the recipient gets amount minus a fee up to maxFee.
findings.evidence: TokenMessengerV2._handleReceiveMessage: _mintAndWithdraw(..., _amount - _fee, _fee); _validatedReceivedMessage requires _fee <= maxFee. Case 3 screen: "Bridge 42 USDC to domain 0" with a separate field "Max fee 0.0042 USDC".
findings.fix: Relabel maxFee as "Max fee (deducted from amount)", or add to the intent: "Bridge {amount} to {destinationDomain}, fee up to {maxFee}".

findings.title: depositForBurn: mint recipient and destination caller shown as raw bytes32, which are hard to compare with an address.
findings.evidence: definitions.mintRecipient and definitions.destinationCaller use format raw. Case 2 screen: "0x000000000000000000000000dad77910dbdfde764fc21fcd4e74d71bbaca6d8d". A [-20:] slice with addressName would cut non-EVM recipients (Solana, Stellar), so no single format fits every domain.
findings.fix: Keep raw, or add a hint in the label such as "Mint recipient (last 20 bytes = EVM address)".

findings.title: depositForBurn: minFinalityThreshold is hidden, so the signer can't see whether this is a fast or standard transfer.
findings.evidence: descriptor field {"path":"minFinalityThreshold","visible":"never"}. Cases 2 and 3 use 0x7d0 (2000, standard). The fee stays within the maxFee that is shown.
findings.fix: Optionally show it with an enum {1000: Fast, 2000: Standard}.

formats.key: depositForBurnWithHook(uint256 amount, uint32 destinationDomain, bytes32 mintRecipient, address burnToken, bytes32 destinationCaller, uint256 maxFee, uint32 minFinalityThreshold, bytes hookData)
effects: `amount` of burnToken (USDC) moves from the signer to the local TokenMinter through transferFrom, using the signer's allowance to TokenMessengerV2, and is burned on Polygon.
On destinationDomain, mintRecipient is minted `amount` minus the fee charged (at most maxFee).
hookData goes into the burn message, and the destination recipient or forwarder interprets it. In case 0 it names the final Stellar account that the forwarder pays.
Only destinationCaller can relay the message on the destination chain. bytes32(0) means anyone can.
minFinalityThreshold sets fast or standard attestation and the fee charged, which stays within maxFee.
formats.shown: Bridge <amount USDC> to domain <number>, with the amount, the raw domain, the raw bytes32 recipient, the max fee, the raw destination caller and the raw hook data hex.

findings.title: depositForBurnWithHook: destination domain shown as a bare CCTP number (27, 3) instead of a chain name.
findings.evidence: definitions.destination format raw. Case 0 screen: "Bridge 25 USDC to domain 27". Case 1: "Bridge 1250.5 USDC to domain 3" (Arbitrum).
findings.fix: Use an enum of CCTP domains (3 Arbitrum, 6 Base, 27 Stellar, …) with format enum, and put it in the intent.

findings.title: depositForBurnWithHook: the intent implies the full amount arrives, but the recipient is minted amount minus a fee up to maxFee.
findings.evidence: TokenMessengerV2._handleReceiveMessage mints _amount - _fee, with _fee <= maxFee. Case 1 screen: "Bridge 1250.5 USDC to domain 3" with a separate "Max fee 0.125 USDC".
findings.fix: Label maxFee "Max fee (deducted from amount)" or mention it in the interpolated intent.

findings.title: depositForBurnWithHook: the final beneficiary in the hook data is only visible as raw hex.
findings.evidence: Case 0: mintRecipient = destinationCaller = 0x72bd20ff… (a forwarder). Hook data hex is ASCII for "GCNHC2KY3QLJYXJCTY64TWDFHZWMOUYRD6AGMWUZOSK2VHK7D5MYUYZA", the Stellar account that finally gets the funds. Field {"path":"hookData","format":"raw"}.
findings.fix: No ERC-7730 format decodes the hook payload. Mention in the description or intent of forwarder-specific descriptors that the hook carries the final recipient.

findings.title: depositForBurnWithHook: mint recipient and destination caller shown as raw bytes32.
findings.evidence: definitions.mintRecipient and definitions.destinationCaller use format raw. Case 1: "0x000000000000000000000000dad77910dbdfde764fc21fcd4e74d71bbaca6d8d". Case 0 uses a non-EVM 32-byte recipient, so a [-20:] address slice would be wrong.
findings.fix: Keep raw, or add a label hint for EVM domains.

findings.title: depositForBurnWithHook: minFinalityThreshold hidden, so fast or standard transfer isn't stated.
findings.evidence: field {"path":"minFinalityThreshold","visible":"never"}. Cases 0 and 1 use 2000. The fee is bounded by the maxFee shown.
findings.fix: Optionally show it with an enum {1000: Fast, 2000: Standard}.
